By the authority vested in me as President o f the U nited States o f Am erica by 
the Agricultural Trade Developm ent and A ssistan ce A c t o f 1954, as am ended 
(7 U .S .C . 1691, e t se q .) and Section 301 o f Title 3 o f the U nited States Code, 
and in order to provide for the delegation o f certain functions to the United 
States International Developm ent Cooperation A gen cy and to revise existing 
delegations, it is hereby ordered as follow s:
1-1. Departm ent o f Agriculture.
1-101. Except as otherwise provided in this Order, the follow ing functions 
vested in the President by the Agricultural Trade Developm ent and A ssistance 
A c t o f 1954, as am ended (hereinafter referred to as the A ct), are delegated to 
the Secretary o f Agriculture: Titles I and IV  (7 U .S .C . 1701, e t s e q ., and 1731, et 
s e q .) .
1-102. The Secretary of Agriculture shall transmit the reports required by the 
provisions o f paragraph 5 of the A c t o f A ugust 13, 1957 (71 Stat. 345; 7 U .S .C . 
1704a).
1- 103. The Secretary of Agriculture, after consultation with the Secretary of 
State, the Secretary o f the Treasury, the Director o f the United States Interna­
tional Developm ent Cooperation A gen cy, the Chairm an o f the Council of 
Econom ic A dvisers; the Director of the O ffice  o f M anagem ent and Budget, and 
the A ssistant to the President for N ational Security A ffairs, shall transmit to 
the Congress all reports required by Section 408 o f the A c t (7 U .S .C , 1736b).
1-2. United States International Developm ent Cooperation A gency.
1-201. Adm inistration of Title II. The functions vested in the President by Title 
II o f the A c t (7 U .S .C . 1721, et se q .) are delegated to the Director of the United 
States International Developm ent Cooperation A gency.
1-202. O ther functions.
(a) The functions vested in the President by the A c t o f negotiating and 
entering into agreements with friendly countries are delegated to the Director 
o f 1he United States International Developm ent Cooperation A gen cy. Such 
functions shall be exercised in accord with Section 112b of Title I of the 
United States Code and applicable regulations and procedures o f the D epart­
ment of State.
(b) The functions delegated to the Director o f the U nited States International 
Developm ent Cooperation A gency by subsection (a) o f this section are exclu­
sive o f any functions under Section 104 o f the A c t (7 U .S .C . 1704) that are 
delegated to any other agency by this Order and o f functions under Section 
310 of the A ct (7 U .S .C . 1692).
(c) The functions delegated by this Order to the Director o f the U nited States 
International Developm ent Cooperation A gen cy m ay be redelegated to the 
head of any other Executive agency.
1-3. Departm ent of State.
■ 1-301. The Secretary of State shall perform the function o f determining which 
countries are friendly countries within the m eaning o f Section 103(d) of the 
A c t (7 U .S .C . 1703(d)).

with respect to Section 104(e) o f the A c t and to the Director o f the O ffice  of 
M anagem ent and Budget in all other respects.

purchase, custody, deposit, transfer and sale o f foreign currencies received 
under the A ct.
1-403. The provisions o f Sections 1-401 and 1-402 o f this Order shall not limit 
Sections 1-202 and 1-3 o f this Order. The provisions o f Section 1-402 o f this 
Order shall not limit Section 1-401 o f this Order.

U .S .C . 1704) shall be carried out as follow s:

the Director of the O ffice  o f M anagem ent and Budget m ay designate after 
appropriate consultation;
(2) Those with respect to programs o f culture and educational development, 
health, nutrition, and sanitation by the Director o f the International Com m uni­
cations A gency, the Departm ent o f State, and the head of any other appropri­

(3) A ll others by such agency or agencies as the Director o f the O ffice of

(4) The term “ appropriate consultation” shall include consultation with the

(e) Those under paragraph (b)(4) by the Departm ent o f State and any other

International Developm ent Cooperation A gency.
(h) Those under paragraph (j) by the Departm ent o f the Treasury in consulta­
tion with the Departm ent of State.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 adds to section 1 of Executive Order 10900 a subsection (d) under which the Secretary of Agriculture, after consultation, "shall transmit" to the Congress "all reports required by Section 408 of the Act". Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md the added subsection continues as part of Executive Order 10900 until that order ends. Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980, section 1-501, revokes Executive Order 10900 as amended, and is effective on signing, so the first end is June 27, 1980 (actor: the President by Executive Order 12220; mechanism: express revocation of the amended parent). Executive Order 12220 reissues the reporting direction in its own text, which is a separate command and not a continuation of this clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 amends Executive Order 10900 by revoking "Section 5 thereof and redesignating Sections 6, 7 and 8" as sections 5, 6 and 7. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md the amendment continues as part of Executive Order 10900 until that order ends, which Executive Order 12220, section 1-501, effected on June 27, 1980 by revoking Executive Order 10900 as amended. The alternative reading, that this one-time instruction was exhausted when executed on January 19, 1977, is disclosed for the reviewer; the later date is used for consistency with the amendment ruling and does not change the order-level end because section 1 also ends on June 27, 1980.

THE PRESIDENT 4325
Executive Order 11963 • January 19, 1977
Delegating Reporting Functions Under the Agricultural Trade Development  
and Assistance Act of 1954, as Amended
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 408 of the Agricultural Trade 
Development and Assistance Act of 1954, as amended (7 U.S.G. 1736b), Section 301

it is hereby ordered as follows:

ing to Section 1  thereof a,new subsection (d) as follows:

State, Secretary of the Treasury, Administrator of the Agency for International 
Development, Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers, Director of the Office 
of Management and Budget, Chairman of the Council on International Economic 
Policy and the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs, shall transmit 
to the Congress all reports required by Section 408 of the Act (7 U.S.C. 1736b, 
1970 ed., Supp. V ) -

voking Section 5 thereof and redesignating Sections 6, 7 and 8 as Sections 5, 6 and

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11963 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4325) has two sections, both amending Executive Order 10900 of January 5, 1961 (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954): section 1 adds a subsection (d) to section 1 of Executive Order 10900 directing the Secretary of Agriculture, after consultation with named officials, to transmit to the Congress the reports required by section 408 of the Act, and section 2 revokes section 5 of Executive Order 10900 and redesignates sections 6, 7 and 8 as 5, 6 and 7. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md an amendment continues, as part of the amended order, until the parent order ends. Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980 (45 FR 44245), section 1-501, revokes Executive Order 10900 as amended; it takes effect on signing and states no later date. That is the first end for both sections. The same reporting direction is reissued independently in Executive Order 12220, so the function continues under a different order. The reading that section 2, an instruction executed when issued, was exhausted on January 19, 1977 and only its consequence survived is the alternative a reviewer should see; it would not change the order-level end date of June 27, 1980, which is set by section 1. The 7 U.S.C. 1691 note in the U.S. Code release point 119-121 lists this order as an amending order of Executive Order 10900 and carries that order's ended status line.

Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF JOSEPH W. AusTIN From ComMPpuLsoRY RETIREMENT FOR
AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S. C.,
sec. 715a), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or
service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District
of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that Joseph W. Austin, foreman
carpenter in the United States Capitol Building under the office of the Architect of
the Capitol, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of two years
by Executive Order No. 6976 of February 26, 1935, be further exempted from the
provisions of this section and continued in the service until March 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Joseph W. Austin from the provisions
thereof and continue him in the service until March 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THe Wuite Houss,
February 27, 1937.

[No. 7565]

U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1997

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THe Wuite Houss,
February 27, 1937.

[No. 7565]
